chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who performs salat (prayer) while her hands are bound with henna. He said: If she had performed wudu (ablution) for the salat (prayer) before that, then there is no harm in the salat (prayer) while she is dyed with henna and her hands are bound.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman about whom the legal ruling is asked
key_terms.بِالْحِنَّاءِ: with henna applied to the hands
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مَرْبُوطَتَانِ: wrapped or bound, referring to the hands being covered for henna

ai.seo_question: Can a woman perform salat (prayer) with henna on her hands if she already performed wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman praying while henna is applied to her hands in a wrapped state. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that if she had already performed wudu (ablution) before that, then her salat (prayer) is valid and there is no problem.
